payload.claim: The round-trip witness for criterion 1 strips every column whose name ends in `_id` before comparing folded rows to the writer's rows (`_compact`, line 52-57). That filter is meant to drop surrogate keys like `task_id`/`attempt_id`, but `tasks.spec_id` also ends in `_id` and is a real, NOT-derived business column written by `task_created`. It is silently excluded from every comparison in this file, including the final 'no compared column is NULL' assertion, so nothing in `test_every_task_fact_kind_folds_back_to_the_rows_its_write_made` (or the second-task check at the end of that test) verifies `spec_id` survives the fold. Changing `_apply`'s `task_created` insert to write the wrong `spec_id` would leave this witness green even though criterion 1 explicitly claims a 'column for column' rebuild. (The legacy `rows()`-based tests in `tests/test_fold.py`, which this spec keeps only until the second spec removes them, do still catch a `spec_id` regression today, but the criterion-1 witness that is supposed to be the authoritative round trip does not.)
